label: rare late-input / <DEL> feature in sequences starting with j or g (weak tendency)
explanation: Extremely sparse: it fires on 0.017% of steps, with weak magnitudes (median 0.12). About half the activation mass falls on late original-phase steps (orig_idx 5-7) and on the <DEL> step, and it is concentrated in sequences whose first token is j or g (about 8-9x lift). Requiring the second token to be in {j, e} raises precision to only about 4%, and adding the third token raises it to about 11% at a large cost in recall. The other quarter of the mass falls in the copy phase, mostly on input g while outputting j or g, also with low precision. In most j/g-initial sequences it does not fire at all (precision about 0.7%), and it never fires at t<3. No predicate tried got above F1 0.12, so the feature looks like a sparse conjunction of specific prefix tokens that these variables cannot capture. Magnitude was not found to follow any variable we checked.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+7.26), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+3.92), orig0=j (+3.58), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+3.30), orig1=j (+3.03), orig0=g (+2.94). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.10), prev3_tok=- (-3.95), recall_idx=1 (-3.06), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.06).
